- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment events.
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is strongly negative; model fails to fully reflect bearish sentiment.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to over- or under-forecasting in mid-term horizon.
- High sentiment volatility → model overfits short-term noise; reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment swings > -0.5 or > 0.5.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast growth rate by 10–15% to account for downward bias.
- If model forecast > true outcome by > 1.5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward adjustment to next forecast.
- For sentiment > 0.3, model tends to overpredict; for sentiment < -0.3, underpredict — apply sentiment-weighted correction factor.
